title: Tuberosity-alveolar block as a donor site for localised augmentation of the maxilla: a retrospective clinical study
authors: Khojasteh A, Nazeman P, Tolstunov L. Br J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2016; 54(8):950-955.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “Retrospective assessment of the efficacy of tuberosity-alveolar block bone (posterior maxillary alveolar ridge) in the augmentation of adjacent defects in the maxilla using data from 14 patients (10 men and four women, mean (range) age 55 (38-69) years) who had had 20 bony augmentations with block bone from the al veolar tuberosity during 2014. Patients were divided into three groups according to the technique by which the bone was collected. The first group had a graft from the alveolar tuberosity covered with titanium mesh (titanium mesh group); the second group h ad the block bone covered by platelet rich fibrin and collagen membrane (platelet rich fibrin group), and in the third group the graft was covered only with periosteum (periosteum group).
